```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
source("../_common.R")

russell_career <- tibble(
  season = c("1956-57", "1957-58", "1958-59", "1959-60", "1960-61", "1961-62",
             "1962-63", "1963-64", "1964-65", "1965-66", "1966-67", "1967-68", "1968-69"),
  ppg = c(14.7, 16.6, 16.7, 18.2, 16.9, 18.9, 16.8, 15.0, 14.1, 12.9, 13.3, 12.5, 9.9),
  rpg = c(19.6, 22.7, 23.0, 24.0, 23.9, 23.6, 23.6, 24.7, 24.1, 22.8, 21.0, 18.6, 19.3),
  championship = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)
)

champions_comparison <- tibble(
  player = c("Bill Russell", "Michael Jordan", "Kareem Abdul-Jabbar", "Magic Johnson", "LeBron James"),
  rings = c(11, 6, 6, 5, 4)
)
```

> *"The most important measure of how good a game I played was how much better I'd made my teammates play."* – Bill Russell

## The Invisible Scoreboard

Bill Russell won 11 NBA championships in 13 seasons. That's not a typo. Eleven. In thirteen years.

Yet if you only looked at his scoring statistics, you might wonder what the fuss was about. Russell averaged just 15.1 points per game for his career—modest by superstar standards.

**The difference was that Russell measured success by a different scoreboard—one that counted wins, not points.**

## Defense Wins Championships

In an era before blocks were officially tracked, Russell was estimated to have blocked over 8,000 shots in his career. He transformed defense from an afterthought into an art form.

```{r championship-rings, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Russell's 11 championships remain unmatched in NBA history"

highchart() %>%
  hc_chart(type = "bar") %>%
  hc_title(text = "Championship Rings: Russell vs. Other Legends") %>%
  hc_xAxis(categories = champions_comparison$player) %>%
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Championships"), max = 12) %>%
  hc_add_series(
    name = "Rings",
    data = champions_comparison$rings,
    colorByPoint = TRUE,
    colors = c("#007A33", "#CE1141", "#552583", "#552583", "#860038")
  ) %>%
  hc_plotOptions(bar = list(dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE))) %>%
  hc_add_theme(hc_theme_flatdark())
```

## The Team-First Mentality

Russell didn't chase individual statistics. He chased wins. His rebounding wasn't about padding numbers—it was about giving his teammates extra possessions.

```{r rebounding-dominance, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Russell's rebounding was consistently dominant throughout his career"

highchart() %>%
  hc_chart(type = "areaspline") %>%
  hc_title(text = "Bill Russell: Career Rebounding") %>%
  hc_subtitle(text = "Averaged over 20 rebounds per game for most of his career") %>%
  hc_xAxis(categories = russell_career$season, labels = list(rotation = -45)) %>%
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Rebounds Per Game"), min = 0, max = 30) %>%
  hc_add_series(name = "RPG", data = russell_career$rpg, color = "#007A33", fillOpacity = 0.3) %>%
  hc_add_theme(hc_theme_flatdark())
```

## Leadership Under Pressure

Russell was 10-0 in Game 7s. Perfect. When everything was on the line, Russell delivered—not with heroic shots, but with smothering defense, timely rebounds, and plays that don't show up in box scores.

| Achievement | Value |
|------------|-------|
| Championships | 11 |
| MVP Awards | 5 |
| Game 7 Record | 10-0 |
| Career Rebounds | 21,620 |
| All-Star Games | 12 |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Lessons from Russell's Invisible Impact

1. **Redefine success metrics** - Wins matter more than individual stats
2. **Make others better** - Russell's presence elevated his entire team
3. **Defense is a mindset** - He turned it into a weapon, not a chore
4. **Show up in big moments** - His Game 7 record speaks for itself
:::
